newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai March cash balance remains in deficit. [CORRECTED 08:21 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Thai March cash balance remains in deficit. [CORRECTED 08:21 GMT]

text.p: Thailand's cash balance in March remained in deficit, finance minister Amnuay Viravan (Corrects from deputy finance minister Thawatwongse Na Chiang Mai) said on Wednesday.
Thailand recorded a 45 billion baht deficit in the cash balance as of February.
However, Amnuay said the central bank projected that Thailand will record a surplus in the cash balance for this fiscal year as the situation in the second half of the year is expected to improve.
The minister also said that the exports in February contracted 5.5 percent year on year mostly due to a drop in agricultural commodities, not industrial goods.
"The prices of rubber and tapioca have dropped during the month. Though the prices of rice are very strong, we exported less than last year," he said.
"This does not mean that our rice is not competitive. It's just the matter of timing. People are on a wait-and-see stance before the second crop rice entered the market,' he said.
He also attributed sluggish trade in February to long holidays in the month.
Amnuay's figure of 5.5 percent contraction in exports differed slightly from that released earlier by his deputy Thawatwongse Na Chiang Mai.
